tracks.narration: Push current through an inductor — where does the energy go?
Close the switch and the current ramps from zero up to I. A magnetic field grows around the coil, and the inductor pushes back with a voltage v equal to L times the rate of change of current.
Plot flux against current. Φ equals L times i — a straight line. The work to push the current from zero up to I is the area under that line, a triangle with area one half L I squared.
Three faces of the same energy: one half L I squared, one half Φ I, and Φ squared over two L. Use whichever two quantities you know.
The energy lives in the magnetic field around the coil. Open the switch and the field collapses — releasing every joule back into the circuit.
